D.treatment: lowest 5% of schools by spring reading achievement

O.outcome_detail: median student growth percentile from fall to spring

cells.quote: Assuming the intent of ESSA is to provide comprehensive support to schools and students where little learning is going on, 77% of the lowest 5% achieving schools based on spring reading achievement grow their typical student better than the 30th percentile (about 0.5 standard deviations below the mean).
cells.note: The study reports an observational comparison of schools; the 30th percentile is a growth benchmark rather than a separate randomized comparison group.

D.treatment: ESSA plan includes a postsecondary readiness indicator
D.comparison: ESSA plan does not include one

O.outcome_detail: Presence of a postsecondary readiness indicator as a scoring element

cells.quote: In total, 41 out of 53 ESSA plans (77%) included a postsecondary readiness indicator as a scoring element that contributed to identifying schools for additional support.
cells.note: Descriptive document comparison; no causal treatment was assigned.

O.outcome_detail: Prevalence of measure types among plans with a postsecondary readiness indicator

result.effect: Academic measures: 40 states (98%); military measures: 11 states (27%)

cells.quote: Nearly every ESSA plan that included a postsecondary readiness indicator incorporated an academically-focused measure, such as meeting a minimum score on the SAT or ACT or completing advanced or dual enrollment coursework. However, only 27 percent of plans explicitly had a military-focused measure, such as achieving a threshold score on the ASVAB exam or enlisting in a military branch (see Table 2).
cells.note: Descriptive comparison of coded measure prevalence; not an experimental contrast.

O.outcome_detail: Percentage weight of the postsecondary readiness indicator in the summative accountability score

cells.quote: Weighting ranged from a high of 33 percent in Louisiana to a low of five percent in Michigan.
cells.note: Descriptive document comparison; the states were not assigned to weighting conditions.

D.treatment: postsecondary readiness indicator with the most measures

O.outcome_detail: Number of separate measures used to calculate the indicator

result.effect: 23 measures in North Dakota versus 1 measure in Oregon, Pennsylvania, and Puerto Rico

cells.quote: Postsecondary readiness indicators also varied in complexity, with states including anywhere from 1 (Oregon, Pennsylvania, and Puerto Rico) to 23 (North Dakota) separate measures to calculate postsecondary readiness (see Figure 3).
cells.note: Descriptive document comparison of indicator complexity; no causal inference is warranted.

cells.quote: An Education Week survey reveals that 77 percent of school principals and district leaders across the nation reported challenges in hiring enough substitutes during the pandemic, shortages that have been more challenging than those of any other staffing positions (including bus drivers, full-time teachers, paraprofessionals, and custodians).
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive survey comparison; no intervention, learning population, setting, duration, or printed effect size is stated.
